business: All Brunswick Van Lines / All Brunswick Moving & Storage

opportunities.title: Photo/video survey-to-estimate agent: room-by-room inventory, cubic-foot/weight roll-up and written estimate draft
opportunities.problem: Every quote depends on a manual in-home walkthrough that produces a hand-built inventory, and the weight-based estimate is the fault line in the company's reputation: one 2025 one-star review says the weight estimate was badly low and disputes the final cost, while other reviewers report the final bill at or below estimate. An older moving-forum thread shows the same estimate-basis and valuation-coverage confusion. With 4 power units and 6 drivers, a re-survey or a variance dispute burns scarce estimator and crew hours, and the survey step is a single-person dependency - reviewers name the estimator personally.
evidence: Customers must submit a web form so a salesperson can schedule a free in-home survey, and a detailed inventory is produced before loading - no instant or self-serve estimate path: https://allbrunswick.com/request-a-quote/

A 2025 one-star Yelp review disputes the final cost as far above a weight-based estimate, while other reviews say the final bill came in at or below estimate: https://www.yelp.com/biz/all-brunswick-van-lines-dayton-8
An older moving-forum thread raised the same estimate-basis and valuation-coverage confusion for an interstate move: https://www.movingscam.com/forum/viewtopic.php?t=21080

Angi reviewers credit an in-home estimator by name for the walk-through, i.e. estimate quality rests on one or two people: https://www.angi.com/companylist/us/nj/dayton/all-brunswick-van-lines-inc-reviews-2091594.htm
Fleet/crew base is thin relative to review volume - 4 trucks, 2 tractors, 6 drivers, ~100,000 miles in 2025: https://www.lanefinder.com/c/all_brunswick_van_lines/866526
opportunities.agent_design: Trigger: quote-form submission or a survey appointment is created. The estimator (or the customer, pre-visit) walks the home with a phone recording video or a sequence of photos; a vision agent itemizes furniture and box counts by room, codes each item to a standard household-goods inventory library with a cubic-foot value, rolls the inventory up to cubic feet and an estimated weight band, and flags high-variance items (piano, gym equipment, packed garage/basement, storage add-ons) that need a human look. It then drafts the written estimate package plus the customer-facing inventory sheet. Systems touched: WordPress quote form, shared sales@ inbox, survey calendar, PDF/estimate template, storage-warehouse inventory list for goods going into the South Brunswick site. Human approval: the estimator reviews and edits item codes and the cubic-foot/weight total and signs the estimate before it reaches the customer; anything with a projected variance above a set threshold routes to Steve Morgen. Pricing math stays in a deterministic calculator, not in the model.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: This needs vision plus a moving-specific item library, deterministic cubic-foot/weight arithmetic, and a versioned estimate record the carrier can reproduce if a customer disputes the bill. A chatbot subscription cannot read a walkthrough video, cannot write into the quote pipeline, and leaves no auditable trail - so it cannot defend a weight-based charge or reduce re-surveys.

impact_estimate.range: $9,000-$35,000/yr in estimator hours returned plus avoided estimate-variance write-downs
impact_estimate.assumptions: 12-25 surveys/month (inference: ~385 estimated monthly site visits per Crunchbase modelling plus a 4-truck/6-driver crew that caps job volume) at 1.5-2.5 survey-and-write-up hours each, costed at the NJ mean wage for Cargo & Freight Agents ($28.80/hr, $59,360/yr) and tractor-trailer drivers ($30.04/hr median) as surveyor proxies. Agent removes 30-45% of the documentation portion = roughly $3,000-$11,000. Separately, 2-5 jobs/yr where a low estimate is caught before move day, avoiding $1,500-$4,000 of absorbed cost each = $3,000-$20,000 (inference - the company publishes no pricing or tariff, so per-job revenue is assumed, not sourced). Lower bound assumes 12 surveys/month and 30% time removal.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 3-4 weeks: vision-to-inventory pipeline validated on 10-15 real past surveys re-run from photos/video, a cubic-foot/weight calculator tuned to their own historical estimates, and a room-by-room PDF inventory plus estimate draft. Deliverable includes measured item-coding accuracy against the estimator's own written inventory and minutes saved per survey.

opportunities.title: After-hours intake and survey-booking agent that unifies the WordPress quote form and the Wheaton ballpark-estimate widget
opportunities.problem: All quoting funnels through an office callback: the site asks for a form submission so a salesperson can schedule a survey, hours are Mon-Fri 8:00-17:00 with weekends closed, and there is no online booking, live chat, after-hours line or online payment - the only published channels are two phone lines, a fax and one shared sales@ inbox. Lead capture is also split across two systems, the WordPress form and Wheaton's separate 'Ballpark Estimate 2023' widget. A household mover's inquiries concentrate in evenings and weekends when people plan a move, so demand that lands after 5pm Friday waits until Monday and is frequently lost to a competitor who answers instantly.
evidence: Quote capture is a generic WordPress form that promises an office callback to schedule a free in-home survey - no calendar, no instant price: https://allbrunswick.com/request-a-quote/
Published hours are Mon-Fri 8:00-17:00, Saturday and Sunday closed, with no published after-hours or emergency line: https://www.mapquest.com/us/new-jersey/all-brunswick-van-lines-1054888
Contact surface is a main line, toll-free line, fax and one shared sales@ inbox rather than department queues; no live chat or online payment is listed: https://allbrunswick.com/aboutus/

A second, separate lead-capture path runs on the Wheaton agent page via a 'Ballpark Estimate 2023' widget, so inquiries arrive in two places: https://www.wheatonworldwide.com/find-a-local-agent/agents/all-brunswick-van-lines-inc

Peak-season crew hiring runs continuously ('hiring drivers and helpers immediately'), implying inbound demand spikes the office must absorb with the same small staff: https://www.facebook.com/allbrunswick/videos/we-are-hiring-drivers-and-helpers-immediatelylocation-central-new-jersey-competi/1089686394233500
opportunities.agent_design: A voice agent answers the main and toll-free numbers outside 8-5 and overflows when the office is on another call, and a matching web-chat agent sits on the quote, storage and contact pages. It qualifies move date window, origin/destination ZIPs, home size, access constraints (stairs, elevators, long carry), storage need and senior/downsizing context. Ballpark ranges come only from a rules table the owners maintain (no free-form model-generated pricing); it offers real in-home survey slots from the office calendar, writes a structured lead into one queue with source attribution (WP form vs Wheaton widget vs phone), sends a confirmation plus a what-to-pack-yourself checklist, and escalates large, urgent or upset callers to an on-call person. Human approval: any quote outside the rules table, any binding commitment, and any complaint routes to a person; the office reviews a next-morning lead digest and can override bookings.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: This is telephony plus after-hours routing, calendar booking, deduplication of two lead sources, and durable lead records with source attribution - with pricing pinned to a deterministic table so the agent never invents a number that becomes a dispute. Off-the-shelf chatbot widgets cannot answer the phone, cannot book a survey, cannot reconcile the Wheaton widget with the WordPress form, and cannot hand the office a clean daily queue.

impact_estimate.range: $8,000-$35,000/yr in office hours plus incremental booked jobs
impact_estimate.assumptions: 5-10 office hours/week currently spent on intake, call-backs and re-explaining the survey process across 46 working weeks, costed at NJ mean wages for dispatchers ($24.32/hr, $26.64/hr mean) and cargo & freight agents ($28.80/hr) = roughly $5,600-$13,000. Demand capture: 25-40% of inquiries arriving outside published hours is an inference from weekend-closed hours plus summer-peak hiring; 2-6 incremental booked jobs/yr at an assumed $1,500-$4,000 average ticket (pricing not published) = $3,000-$24,000. Lower bound assumes 5 hrs/week saved and 2 jobs; no credit taken for faster response improving close rate on in-hours leads.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 3 weeks: after-hours voice and chat agent live on one number plus the WP quote form, rules-table ballpark ranges, survey-calendar booking, and a unified lead queue with source tags. Pilot report counts after-hours and overflow inquiries, surveys booked without staff involvement, and minutes of office time saved per day.

opportunities.title: Move-file and coverage knowledge agent for customers and new crews (valuation terms, paperwork rules, claims documentation)
opportunities.problem: The rules that decide whether a move ends in a five-star review or a cost dispute live with a few named people: reviewers credit individual office staff with guidance on what to pack themselves, and the recurring confusion in public threads is what the estimate is based on and what valuation coverage does and does not pay. That knowledge is also needed by the crews: job ads assign drivers 'accurate completion of paperwork on assigned jobs' alongside taking inventory of every shipment, yet hiring runs through Facebook posts that tell applicants to phone the office, /careers/ returns 404, and no SOP or training library is published. Every seasonal helper therefore re-asks the same paperwork, packing-standard and 'is this covered' questions in peak weeks.
evidence: Job ads assign the driver 'accurate completion of paperwork on assigned jobs' as well as taking inventory of every shipment: https://linkedin.com/company/all-brunswick-van-lines-inc

Hiring is phone-intake only - a Facebook post tells applicants to call (732) 274-1881 - and the site has no careers page (/careers/ returns HTTP 404): https://www.facebook.com/allbrunswick/posts/all-brunswick-moving-storage-is-a-full-service-moving-company-looking-for-full-t/1486874326783502 and https://allbrunswick.com/careers/

Reviewers praise staff for guidance on what to pack themselves and name individual office staff, indicating advice is delivered person-to-person rather than from published material: https://www.angi.com/companylist/us/nj/dayton/all-brunswick-van-lines-inc-reviews-2091594.htm
Estimate-basis and valuation-coverage confusion recurs in a public moving-forum thread about an interstate move with this company: https://www.movingscam.com/forum/viewtopic.php?t=21080
All contact runs through a single shared sales@ inbox, so staff answer the same coverage/packing questions repeatedly: https://allbrunswick.com/aboutus/
opportunities.agent_design: Retrieval agent over the company's own corpus: Wheaton agent tariff and rules extracts, the firm's inventory and paperwork SOPs, packing standards, claims/damage documentation procedure, valuation-coverage explainers, the storage terms (heated, sanitized South Brunswick warehouse) and 12 months of anonymized sales@ email threads. Two front doors: (1) a phone-friendly staff/crew assistant that answers 'what paperwork does this job need', 'how do we document a damaged armoire on delivery', 'how is a garage of paint cans handled', with a citation to the source document; (2) a customer-facing Q&A widget on the quote and storage pages that answers what-to-pack and coverage questions and hands anything about a specific estimate, bill or claim to a person. Human approval: any question naming a specific job, estimate, bill or claim is escalated, the agent never states a coverage dollar amount, and a manager reviews the escalation log weekly and can correct answers.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: The answers have to come from their own tariff, SOPs and email history - much of it PDFs and inbox threads - with citations a manager can stand behind when a customer disputes a charge. A generic chatbot has no access to those documents, will paraphrase coverage terms incorrectly, cannot gate claim-specific questions, and cannot be corrected by the owners.

impact_estimate.range: $4,000-$15,000/yr in staff time plus fewer drawn-out disputes
impact_estimate.assumptions: 3-6 staff hours/week answering repeat coverage, packing-standard and paperwork questions across 46 working weeks at $24.32-$28.80/hr NJ mean (dispatchers / cargo & freight agents) = $3,400-$9,000. Plus 1-3 disputes or re-worked paperwork files per year handled materially faster, at an assumed $1,000-$2,000 of staff and manager time each = $1,000-$6,000 (inference - no internal claim counts available; BBB shows only 1 formal complaint in 3 years, so the complaint volume, not the volume of informal disputes, is what is measured). Crew onboarding time saved is not monetized in this range.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 3 weeks: ingest tariff extracts, SOPs, packing standards and anonymized email threads; build a 60-question evaluation set from real customer and crew questions; ship a staff chat plus a site widget with citation links and an escalation button. Pilot reports answer accuracy against the eval set and how many staff questions the agent absorbed.

lead_score.rationale: Pain (20/30): the process gaps are documented on the company's own site (callback-only quoting, Mon-Fri 8-5 with weekends closed, no online booking or payment, split lead capture between the WordPress form and Wheaton's ballpark widget) and the estimate-accuracy fault line is visible in a 2025 one-star review and a forum thread. But this is not a loud-pain account: BBB shows only 1 complaint in 3 years, Angi is 4.8/57, and no internal wait-time, lead-volume or variance data is public, so the operational cost is inferred from process design rather than measured. Fit (17/20): almost everything sits in capability A (intake, quoting, follow-up) and C (knowledge), with no hardware and no regulated driving-hours work - the risky area (HOS/ELD) is deliberately avoided because an agent cannot author driver hours. Ability to pay (11/20): genuinely small - FMCSA-derived 4 trucks / 2 tractors / 6 drivers, 21 jobs on the 2020 PPP filing, revenue unverified and conflicting (Manta ~$1.65M vs Crunchbase 11-50 staff), so budget is likely low-four-figures monthly; Wheaton corporate programs are the plausible co-funding route. Ease (11/15): single owner-operator decision-maker (Steve Morgen) and a simple stack, but integrations are with a WordPress form and a van-line agent portal rather than open APIs, and the office is phone-first, so adoption effort is real. Strategic (13/15): household-goods movers are a large, homogeneous segment with identical funnels, and Wheaton's 350+ agent network plus other van lines are an obvious referral channel - the estimate and intake agents are close to productizable. Overall 72: strong fit and repeatability, held back by modest size and by pain that is evidenced in public process signals rather than in the firm's own numbers; the first conversation should test whether weekend/evening lost demand is real, since that is the cheapest thing to prove and the fastest ROI to demo.

best_evidence_signal: Quote demand is callback-only and time-boxed - a web form promising an office callback to schedule a survey, Mon-Fri 8-5 hours with weekends closed, and no online booking anywhere in the funnel: https://allbrunswick.com/request-a-quote/
suggested_channel: phone (owner-operator office line listed on their own site, ask for Steve Morgen) - the firm publishes phone, toll-free, fax and one shared sales@ inbox and tells applicants and customers to call, so a call is the native channel; a walk-in at 182 J Ridge Road is the fallback if the office does not answer outside move season
